Position Overview

Kiewit’s Industrial division is seeking a highly driven Engineering Project Manager
to lead multidisciplinary engineering efforts across complex industrial projects. You will guide engineering deliverables from concept through commissioning, ensuring alignment with project objectives, client expectations, and Kiewit’s rigorous standards for safety, quality, and performance.

Location

We prefer the role to be located in our Lenexa Kansas (Kansas City), Forworth Texas, Lone Tree Colorado offices. Remote locations may be considered that are near other Kiewit major offices but with 50% travel to Lenexa Kansas required, for more Senior level candidates with 12+ years of Engineering PM experience in one or more of our specific industries.

Lead and manage all multi-disciplined engineering activities for assigned industrial projects, ensuring deliverables are completed on schedule, within scope, and to Kiewit quality standards from design into construction administration.
Coordinate cross‑functional engineering disciplines, construction teams, and external partners to maintain alignment and resolve technical challenges.
Oversee development, review, and approval of engineering documents, including drawings, specifications, calculations, and technical reports.
Drive early project planning, design development, and constructability reviews to optimize cost, schedule, and execution strategy.
Manage engineering budgets, forecasts, progress tracking, and change management processes.
Serve as the primary technical liaison with clients, vendors, and internal stakeholders, including our Construction project manager/team, ensuring clear communication and timely issue resolution.
Champion Kiewit’s commitment to safety, innovation, and continuous improvement across all engineering activities.
Support proposal development, estimating, and project pursuit efforts with engineering expertise and strategic input.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Chemical, or related discipline) is required.
5+ years of engineering design experience for D/B, Progressive D/B or EPC projects within the industrial market such as Industrial Power, Data Centers, Water/Wastewater, Mission Critical Facilities, Mining and Metals, or other similar heavy industrial facilities and at least 2 years of experience leading industrial projects.

Must have demonstrated experience with D/B, Progressive D/B, or EPC project execution, design development, and construction integration.
Excellent communication, leadership, and problem‑solving skills.
Ability to work collaboratively in a fast‑paced environment with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.

Why Kiewit Industrial

Kiewit offers the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging and rewarding industrial projects in North America. Our Engineering Project Managers play a pivotal role in shaping project outcomes, driving innovation, and delivering world‑class results. If you’re motivated by technical leadership, cross‑disciplinary collaboration, and building projects that make an impact, this role is a strong fit.

Communicate and interact effectively and professionally with supervisors, employees, and others individually or in a team environment

Position Description & Qualifications

We’re seeking a dynamic and experienced Project Manager to join Serco’s Naval Acquisition and Sustainment Operation (NASO). A successful candidate will assume a critical role in overseeing and leading engineering and technical services to support maintenance and planning for the overhaul and repair equipment and systems associated with U.S. Navy Surface Ships. This position will be located in Everett, WA.

This position is contingent upon your ability to maintain your DoD Secret level clearance.

Serco’s Naval Acquisition and Sustainment Operation is part of our high-performing Maritime, Engineering, Technology, and Sustainment Business Unit which provides critical services to nearly all U.S. Navy surface ships, submarines and craft and is achieving truly impactful outcomes. Serco has over 9,000 people in North America, with operations across the U.S. and Canada. We are committed to forming long-term partnerships and supporting Federal and State government customers to achieve their mission.

In This Role You Will

Lead teams providing technical guidance to Ship's Force relating to work on Hull, Mechanical & Electrical (HM&E) and aviation equipment and systems which interface with combat support systems, and hull support items such as damage control equipment for flooding and fire, climate control/ventilation systems, tank and voids, plenums, etc., habitability improvements, and piping systems. Also encompassed are electrical generation, power and distribution systems including controllers, junction boxes, cabling, and cableways.
Lead the performance of inspections, examinations, analysis, repairs incidental to such and make recommendations in the areas of maintenance planning and/or repair as requested on naval propulsion and auxiliary machinery associated with high pressure steam propulsion plants and U.S. Naval Surface Force Ship propulsion plants and auxiliaries.
Liaison with ship’s reactor department is required prior to accomplishing inspections, testing, and production work
Manage teams performing, assisting, or providing technical guidance on the performance of fault identification and support Ship's Force with physical repairs of the types of naval propulsion and auxiliary and aviation/flight deck equipment/combat systems and systems set forth herein
Responsible for technical support and advice to Ship's Force pertinent to the operation, overhaul, and repair of specific items of, auxiliary machinery, electrical, and hull support and aviation systems as directed by the appropriate technical authority.
Oversee the performance or provide guidance IAW Corrosion Control Assessment and Maintenance Manual (CCAMM) for the Maintenance System Work Package Planning (MSWP) (T-9630-ABMMD-010/all USN hulls) to Ship's Force with training, inspection and reporting of tanks, voids, plenums, bilges, catwalks, pump room decks, and Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF) station decks. Perform or provide technical guidance in support of TYCOM Cableway Improvement Program (CIP) in accordance with NAVSEAINST 9304 series to Ship's Force with training, inspection, repair assistance and reporting.
Develop updated training package to the TYCOM and to the RMCs. Provide formal on-board operator and maintenance training to Ship’s Force.
Develop Formal Work Packages (FWPs) and Controlled Work Packages (CWPs) in accordance with the Joint Fleet Maintenance Manual.
Manage personnel as required to support short-term and long-term contract efforts.
Cultivating positive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.

To Be Successful In This Role, You Will Have

Bachelor's Degree with a minimum of seven years’ experience in related engineering management field, or Associates Degree with fourteen (14) years’ experience in related engineering management field.
An active DoD security clearance is required
Five years’ supervisory experience in the area of technical assistance, maintenance, or design related to surface ships.
Three years should be closely involved with practical surface ship maintenance, design, operation, and other problems of main propulsion, auxiliary,electrical, and damage control equipment associated with shipboard level maintenance.
Two years direct experience with auxiliary, electrical, and damage control systems and included steam propulsion plants.
Two years direct experience with auxiliary, electrical and damage control systems for U.S. Naval Ships.

About Coefficient Giving

Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy) is a philanthropic funder and advisor. We work with a range of donors who share our commitment to cost-effective, high-impact giving. Our current funds include Science and Global Health R&D, Navigating Transformative AI, Biosecurity & Pandemic Preparedness, Abundance & Growth, Farm Animal Welfare, and more.

We’re Proud Of Our Track Record

We jump-started the field of AI safety and security and have played a vital role in addressing other existential threats, such as mirror bacteria.
Our grants to evidence-backed global health programs have saved over 100,000 lives, and our farm animal welfare grants have improved the lives of over 3 billion animals.
We supported late-stage clinical trials for the R21 malaria vaccine, now being scaled to protect millions of kids globally.
We were the earliest major funder of the YIMBY movement to build more housing. Our grantees have led the charge on major wins like City of Yes in New York, and SB 79 in California, which will enable hundreds of thousands of new housing units.

Since 2014, we’ve directed over $7 billion in grants as part of our mission to help others as much as we can with the resources available to us. It’s also a pivotal moment for Coefficient Giving: we gave around $1 billion last year, and are on track to more than double our giving this year.

We’re significantly scaling our grantmaking and rapidly growing our team to support it, in part because we expect to see large increases in philanthropic funding flowing into the fields where we work in the coming years. Accelerating now lets us fill cost-effective gaps today, and helps lay the groundwork for new donors to step in as well.

Growth at this pace means the work is fast, ambiguous, and often messy: we need to make big decisions, pivot quickly, and make trade-offs. We think this is a uniquely high-leverage moment, and we’re looking for people who find that energizing.

About The Salesforce Team

Our Salesforce team builds and maintains the systems that power CG’s grantmaking and partnerships operations. Salesforce is our system of record, but it sits within a broader ecosystem of tools — such as Airtable, data pipelines, form tools like FormAssembly and Fillout, and integrations like Ironclad — that together support how grants move from decision through payment. Our org supports over 230 active users, including CG staff and external users. While our record volume is relatively low, our work tends to be high-touch and high-complexity, with heavy customization and a deliberately code-first build. The Salesforce team acts as internal consultants to many teams at CG. We care about understanding the problem as much as we do building the solution, and we’re always looking for ways to remove friction, improve data quality, and make our systems more useful to the people who rely on them.

About The Role

This role involves two primary responsibilities: 1) developing a deep understanding of what CG’s stakeholders need, and 2) building it in Salesforce. On the “Administrator” side, you’d own a meaningful share of our incoming ticket triage rotation and make hands-on declarative updates in Salesforce, working closely with our team. On the “Business Analyst” side, you’d own intake, discovery, and requirements work so that projects have build-ready requirements and get shipped faster. Requests increasingly span Salesforce, other tools like Airtable and Slack, Claude-powered workflows, and manual processes, and you’d help gather requirements for workflows that involve many tools, with a strong understanding of how changes in one may affect connecting workflows.

While we currently expect our ideal candidate to spend 60% of their time on administration and 40% on business analysis, it is possible that the exact balance could shift depending on team needs and the candidate’s particular strengths.

You would join a growing Salesforce team — spanning Eastern, Central, and Brasília time — that meets daily and works closely together. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports. Our system keeps getting more complex as CG grows, which means more to administer, more processes to document, and more opportunities to make how we work better!

What the role involves

Salesforce administration and delivery

Configure and build on platform, delivering enhancements and new features declaratively — e.g. custom objects and fields, validation rules, screen flows, page layouts, permission sets, and complex cross-object formula fields and roll-up summaries.
Own a meaningful share of our incoming ticket triage rotation alongside project work, responding to and resolving inbound tickets (cases) with high autonomy and ownership.
Deploy changes from sandbox to production, working within our DevOps practices and suggesting improvements as you identify them.
Support users through User Acceptance Testing, and help stand up additional testing and signoff processes where needed.
Maintain accurate and helpful documentation of system functionality, including user-facing and team-facing documentation.
Proactively propose enhancements and bug fixes to existing systems and processes.

Business analysis

Own case and project intake, lead discovery sessions, write requirements and level-of-effort estimates, and drive backlog refinement so that there’s always sprint-ready work in the queue.
Work with stakeholders of varying technical familiarity and translate their requests into requirements any member of the team could pick up and deliver, understanding the business problem in depth.
Gather requirements for work that spans multiple systems, understanding the workflows that connect Salesforce with other tools and how changes in one can affect others.
Surface what sits behind a request: technical impact, data integrity considerations, level of effort, and the scalability, maintainability, and user-experience tradeoffs involved. Facilitate productive conversations when a request diverges from what’s best overall, including knowing when something may not belong in Salesforce at all.
Lead the next stage of how we gather and refine requirements, building on the intake process we already have so that requirements are clear up front and late-breaking changes rarely delay delivery of a case or project.
Document business processes, flagging opportunities for improvement as you go.

You might work on

Improving flows or forms that make our grantmaking operations more efficient, such as creating or enhancing a form so that answers land as structured data instead of arriving by email.
Gathering and refining requirements for the new fields and automation behind our expanding partnerships work, running discovery with stakeholders who may not have any experience with Salesforce, and translating what they need into something the team can build.
Running discovery for a cross-system integration and forming opinions on what data should live in Salesforce versus elsewhere and which direction a data sync should run.
Standardizing and automating project intake, requirements gathering, refinement, and approval, so that there’s always sprint-ready work in the backlog and late-breaking changes don’t derail delivery.
Scoping a stakeholder’s Salesforce request and fulfilling it using the best possible set of tools, whether that’s building in Salesforce or exploring other options like a Claude-powered workflow, Airtable view, or process change.

Who might be a good fit

We are looking for an experienced Salesforce professional who pairs the technical skills of a seasoned administrator with a real appetite for understanding, documenting, and improving processes through business analysis.

A Successful Candidate Will Possess Most Of These Qualities

Natural fluency with business processes and how to improve them: You enjoy leading discussions about requirements, translating between people with very different levels of technical familiarity, and documenting clear requirements.
Stakeholder-minded: You work collaboratively with users and stakeholders of varying levels of technical fluency across teams like Operations and Programs. You describe past work in terms of the friction you removed for users, not only the cases you closed.
Familiar across connected systems: You’re at ease gathering requirements for work that spans Salesforce and associated tools. You can help a stakeholder think through whether a request is best met in Salesforce, via Claude, in Airtable, or through a process change and speak to the rough tradeoffs, even if you’re not the one building it.
Collaborative: We are a small team that shares work and leans on each other’s strengths, so you are as comfortable deferring to a colleague as making the call yourself.
Significant hands-on experience with Salesforce: You have 5+ years of hands-to-keyboard configuration and declarative build — for example, custom objects and fields, validation rules, email alerts, screen flows, page layouts and Lightning pages, permission sets, sharing settings, custom metadata types, custom settings, and complex cross-object formula fields and roll-up summaries — and are experienced deploying changes from sandbox to production.
Salesforce certified: Salesforce Certified Administrator, plus at least one of Advanced Administrator or Business Analyst.
High ownership in a fast-paced environment: You thrive when there is a lot in motion. You drive ambitious, under-scoped work to completion and make tradeoff recommendations rather than waiting for perfectly scoped requirements. Priorities shift, and you can rebalance. While this is an in-house role, our team manages many priorities at once and is continuously building something new.
Experienced in a code-first org: While you would not be expected to write Apex, a lot of our automation lives in code rather than in Flow. We’d expect you can read enough of it to understand why a record behaves the way it does and to scope requests knowing the answer may be code rather than declarative configuration.
Experience with, or strong openness to, AI-enabled workflows: You are excited to contribute to our recently implemented Salesforce MCP and iterate quickly on it and surrounding workflows.

Desirable, But Not Required

Additional certifications: Having both Advanced Administrator and Business Analyst certifications rather than just one.
Breadth of exposure: You’ve seen how different teams, stakeholders, or organizations solve similar problems, whether that comes from consulting across multiple orgs or from working extensively in-house at a complex organization with many internal stakeholders and varied processes. Ideally, you’ve had experience in the mission-driven, philanthropic, and/or nonprofit space.
Basic Apex or LWC development experience: Knowing basic Apex or LWC development, or holding a Platform Developer I certification. The more of our code-first build you can engage with or contribute to directly, the better.
Integration experience: Third-party integration experience, especially with systems in our stack (Airtable, Zapier, FormAssembly, Fillout, Ironclad, and our BigQuery-based data infrastructure).

We Expect All Our Staff To

Put our mission first, and act with urgency to help us realize our ambitious goals.
Work to model our operating values of ownership, openness, calibration, and inclusiveness.

The ideal candidate for this position will possess many of the skills and experiences described above. However, there is no such thing as a “perfect” candidate. Above all, we are looking for people motivated to contribute to our mission of helping others as much as we can with the resources available to us. Whatever your background, please apply if this role would make you excited to come to work every day.

About Vanir

Vanir is a proud minority- and woman-owned company, recognized as a national leader in program, project and construction management (PMCM) and real estate development. Since 1964, we have consistently exceeded client expectations. Ranked as a top PMCM firm by Engineering News-Record (ENR) for more than three decades, our award-winning team provides a full range of services to public and private sector clients in the aviation; healthcare; education (K-12 and higher); justice and essential services; science and technology; state and local government; transportation; water and wastewater; energy; and commercial, residential and nonprofit markets.

Job Description

Vanir is always interested in connecting with talented Project Managers for current and future opportunities.

This is a general application and is not associated with a specific current opening or project. By submitting your application, you will be considered for opportunities as they become available based on your experience, qualifications, location, and career interests. A member of our Talent Acquisition team may contact you to learn more about your background and discuss opportunities that may be a good match.

The Project Manager provides the planning, coordination, and direction for project management activities to ensure they meet owner needs, specifications, cost, and schedule, from initial project identification through construction closeout. May supervise office/field administrative staff, project/field engineers, assistant project/construction managers, and other assigned staff.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Primary contact and liaison for owner and principle partner entities for the contract, design, systems, procedures and related deliverables
Develops project specific procedures and documentation, and may consult with Owner on design and construction contracts and related A/E systems for the project
Functional knowledge of contracts, drawings, estimates, and specifications to ensure compliance with construction/project requirements
Obtains, maintains, and manages data, information, communications, and approvals required by project and company requirements between owner, architects, engineers, and other project-related entities
Represents owner, project and related parties in public forums and meetings
Manages project controls, cost, and performance activities and procedures, project logistics, organization, systems and project closeout
Leads in project meetings to include documentation, administration, and tracking of relevant information and statuses
May coordinate, direct, and monitor activities of construction management staff, contractors, engineers, architects, and related performing entities
Manages bid phase services, as may be required by the client
Performs other duties as required

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, or equivalent is required (Extensive relevant project management experience in place of education may be considered)
Minimum of 5 years of experience as a Project Manager is required
Knowledge and application of master planning, A/E solicitation, project development, design-phase management, construction estimating, cost, project controls/scheduling, documentation, engineering/construction principles, contracts and delivery methods are required
Strong computer skills and familiarity with Microsoft Office Suite products, and experience with project-related systems such as Prolog and Primavera are required

Certified Construction Manager preferred

Senior Salesforce Administrator and Business Analyst

About Coefficient Giving

Coefficient Giving (formerly Open Philanthropy) is a philanthropic funder and advisor. We work with a range of donors who share our commitment to cost-effective, high-impact giving. Our current funds include Science and Global Health R&D, Navigating Transformative AI, Biosecurity & Pandemic Preparedness, Abundance & Growth, Farm Animal Welfare, and more.

We’re Proud Of Our Track Record

We jump-started the field of AI safety and security and have played a vital role in addressing other existential threats, such as mirror bacteria.
Our grants to evidence-backed global health programs have saved over 100,000 lives, and our farm animal welfare grants have improved the lives of over 3 billion animals.
We supported late-stage clinical trials for the R21 malaria vaccine, now being scaled to protect millions of kids globally.
We were the earliest major funder of the YIMBY movement to build more housing. Our grantees have led the charge on major wins like City of Yes in New York, and SB 79 in California, which will enable hundreds of thousands of new housing units.

Since 2014, we’ve directed over $7 billion in grants as part of our mission to help others as much as we can with the resources available to us. It’s also a pivotal moment for Coefficient Giving: we gave around $1 billion last year, and are on track to more than double our giving this year.

We’re significantly scaling our grantmaking and rapidly growing our team to support it, in part because we expect to see large increases in philanthropic funding flowing into the fields where we work in the coming years. Accelerating now lets us fill cost-effective gaps today, and helps lay the groundwork for new donors to step in as well.

Growth at this pace means the work is fast, ambiguous, and often messy: we need to make big decisions, pivot quickly, and make trade-offs. We think this is a uniquely high-leverage moment, and we’re looking for people who find that energizing.

About The Salesforce Team

Our Salesforce team builds and maintains the systems that power CG’s grantmaking and partnerships operations. Salesforce is our system of record, but it sits within a broader ecosystem of tools — such as Airtable, data pipelines, form tools like FormAssembly and Fillout, and integrations like Ironclad — that together support how grants move from decision through payment. Our org supports over 230 active users, including CG staff and external users. While our record volume is relatively low, our work tends to be high-touch and high-complexity, with heavy customization and a deliberately code-first build. The Salesforce team acts as internal consultants to many teams at CG. We care about understanding the problem as much as we do building the solution, and we’re always looking for ways to remove friction, improve data quality, and make our systems more useful to the people who rely on them.

About The Role

This role involves two primary responsibilities: 1) developing a deep understanding of what CG’s stakeholders need, and 2) building it in Salesforce. On the “Administrator” side, you’d own a meaningful share of our incoming ticket triage rotation and make hands-on declarative updates in Salesforce, working closely with our team. On the “Business Analyst” side, you’d own intake, discovery, and requirements work so that projects have build-ready requirements and get shipped faster. Requests increasingly span Salesforce, other tools like Airtable and Slack, Claude-powered workflows, and manual processes, and you’d help gather requirements for workflows that involve many tools, with a strong understanding of how changes in one may affect connecting workflows.

While we currently expect our ideal candidate to spend 60% of their time on administration and 40% on business analysis, it is possible that the exact balance could shift depending on team needs and the candidate’s particular strengths.

You would join a growing Salesforce team — spanning Eastern, Central, and Brasília time — that meets daily and works closely together. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports. Our system keeps getting more complex as CG grows, which means more to administer, more processes to document, and more opportunities to make how we work better!

What the role involves

Salesforce administration and delivery

Configure and build on platform, delivering enhancements and new features declaratively — e.g. custom objects and fields, validation rules, screen flows, page layouts, permission sets, and complex cross-object formula fields and roll-up summaries.
Own a meaningful share of our incoming ticket triage rotation alongside project work, responding to and resolving inbound tickets (cases) with high autonomy and ownership.
Deploy changes from sandbox to production, working within our DevOps practices and suggesting improvements as you identify them.
Support users through User Acceptance Testing, and help stand up additional testing and signoff processes where needed.
Maintain accurate and helpful documentation of system functionality, including user-facing and team-facing documentation.
Proactively propose enhancements and bug fixes to existing systems and processes.

Business analysis

Own case and project intake, lead discovery sessions, write requirements and level-of-effort estimates, and drive backlog refinement so that there’s always sprint-ready work in the queue.
Work with stakeholders of varying technical familiarity and translate their requests into requirements any member of the team could pick up and deliver, understanding the business problem in depth.
Gather requirements for work that spans multiple systems, understanding the workflows that connect Salesforce with other tools and how changes in one can affect others.
Surface what sits behind a request: technical impact, data integrity considerations, level of effort, and the scalability, maintainability, and user-experience tradeoffs involved. Facilitate productive conversations when a request diverges from what’s best overall, including knowing when something may not belong in Salesforce at all.
Lead the next stage of how we gather and refine requirements, building on the intake process we already have so that requirements are clear up front and late-breaking changes rarely delay delivery of a case or project.
Document business processes, flagging opportunities for improvement as you go.

You might work on

Improving flows or forms that make our grantmaking operations more efficient, such as creating or enhancing a form so that answers land as structured data instead of arriving by email.
Gathering and refining requirements for the new fields and automation behind our expanding partnerships work, running discovery with stakeholders who may not have any experience with Salesforce, and translating what they need into something the team can build.
Running discovery for a cross-system integration and forming opinions on what data should live in Salesforce versus elsewhere and which direction a data sync should run.
Standardizing and automating project intake, requirements gathering, refinement, and approval, so that there’s always sprint-ready work in the backlog and late-breaking changes don’t derail delivery.
Scoping a stakeholder’s Salesforce request and fulfilling it using the best possible set of tools, whether that’s building in Salesforce or exploring other options like a Claude-powered workflow, Airtable view, or process change.

Who might be a good fit

We are looking for an experienced Salesforce professional who pairs the technical skills of a seasoned administrator with a real appetite for understanding, documenting, and improving processes through business analysis.

A Successful Candidate Will Possess Most Of These Qualities

Natural fluency with business processes and how to improve them: You enjoy leading discussions about requirements, translating between people with very different levels of technical familiarity, and documenting clear requirements.
Stakeholder-minded: You work collaboratively with users and stakeholders of varying levels of technical fluency across teams like Operations and Programs. You describe past work in terms of the friction you removed for users, not only the cases you closed.
Familiar across connected systems: You’re at ease gathering requirements for work that spans Salesforce and associated tools. You can help a stakeholder think through whether a request is best met in Salesforce, via Claude, in Airtable, or through a process change and speak to the rough tradeoffs, even if you’re not the one building it.
Collaborative: We are a small team that shares work and leans on each other’s strengths, so you are as comfortable deferring to a colleague as making the call yourself.
Significant hands-on experience with Salesforce: You have 5+ years of hands-to-keyboard configuration and declarative build — for example, custom objects and fields, validation rules, email alerts, screen flows, page layouts and Lightning pages, permission sets, sharing settings, custom metadata types, custom settings, and complex cross-object formula fields and roll-up summaries — and are experienced deploying changes from sandbox to production.
Salesforce certified: Salesforce Certified Administrator, plus at least one of Advanced Administrator or Business Analyst.
High ownership in a fast-paced environment: You thrive when there is a lot in motion. You drive ambitious, under-scoped work to completion and make tradeoff recommendations rather than waiting for perfectly scoped requirements. Priorities shift, and you can rebalance. While this is an in-house role, our team manages many priorities at once and is continuously building something new.
Experienced in a code-first org: While you would not be expected to write Apex, a lot of our automation lives in code rather than in Flow. We’d expect you can read enough of it to understand why a record behaves the way it does and to scope requests knowing the answer may be code rather than declarative configuration.
Experience with, or strong openness to, AI-enabled workflows: You are excited to contribute to our recently implemented Salesforce MCP and iterate quickly on it and surrounding workflows.

Desirable, But Not Required

Additional certifications: Having both Advanced Administrator and Business Analyst certifications rather than just one.
Breadth of exposure: You’ve seen how different teams, stakeholders, or organizations solve similar problems, whether that comes from consulting across multiple orgs or from working extensively in-house at a complex organization with many internal stakeholders and varied processes. Ideally, you’ve had experience in the mission-driven, philanthropic, and/or nonprofit space.
Basic Apex or LWC development experience: Knowing basic Apex or LWC development, or holding a Platform Developer I certification. The more of our code-first build you can engage with or contribute to directly, the better.
Integration experience: Third-party integration experience, especially with systems in our stack (Airtable, Zapier, FormAssembly, Fillout, Ironclad, and our BigQuery-based data infrastructure).

We Expect All Our Staff To

Put our mission first, and act with urgency to help us realize our ambitious goals.
Work to model our operating values of ownership, openness, calibration, and inclusiveness.

The ideal candidate for this position will possess many of the skills and experiences described above. However, there is no such thing as a “perfect” candidate. Above all, we are looking for people motivated to contribute to our mission of helping others as much as we can with the resources available to us. Whatever your background, please apply if this role would make you excited to come to work every day.

Support enterprise data integration and analysis across facilities portfolios.

Perform GIS and iNFADS data reconciliation to identify discrepancies, validate facility footprints, and align spatial data with official property records.
Integrate financial and property data into geospatial layers, cartographic products, and automated executive dashboards.

Support enterprise-level tracking and analysis of MILCON, UMMC, FSRM, and demolition project execution.

About Vanir

Vanir is a proud minority- and woman-owned company, recognized as a national leader in program, project and construction management (PMCM) and real estate development. Since 1964, we have consistently exceeded client expectations. Ranked as a top PMCM firm by Engineering News-Record (ENR) for more than three decades, our award-winning team provides a full range of services to public and private sector clients in the aviation; healthcare; education (K-12 and higher); justice and essential services; science and technology; state and local government; transportation; water and wastewater; energy; and commercial, residential and nonprofit markets.

Job Description

Vanir is always interested in connecting with talented Project Managers for current and future opportunities.

This is a general application and is not associated with a specific current opening or project. By submitting your application, you will be considered for opportunities as they become available based on your experience, qualifications, location, and career interests. A member of our Talent Acquisition team may contact you to learn more about your background and discuss opportunities that may be a good match.

The Project Manager provides the planning, coordination, and direction for project management activities to ensure they meet owner needs, specifications, cost, and schedule, from initial project identification through construction closeout. May supervise office/field administrative staff, project/field engineers, assistant project/construction managers, and other assigned staff.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Primary contact and liaison for owner and principle partner entities for the contract, design, systems, procedures and related deliverables
Develops project specific procedures and documentation, and may consult with Owner on design and construction contracts and related A/E systems for the project
